speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
text: asked	the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (a) whether there are plans to streamline the grants, funding support and assistance schemes of SPRING Singapore and IE Singapore within the merged entity of Enterprise Singapore; and (b) how will this affect the SMEs that have applied for funding support.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The proposed new agency Enterprise Singapore will build on the good work that has been done by both agencies.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: So, in other words is, we are not waiting for the formation of the new agency to do this.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: This will put us, we believe, in good stead to grow a strong cohort of Singapore companies for our future economy.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The second question is, when the merged entity of Enterprise Singapore exists, would the account management be one single point of contact for all the SMEs?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: As we have emphasised, the formation of the new agency Enterprise Singapore is just one aspect of our overall effort to strengthen our economy and prepare for some of the challenges we anticipate.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And in that regard, the role of the Trade Associations and Chambers (TACs) and, in this case, the specific reference the Member made was to the SME Centres, that remains a very important part of the architecture that we have in our economy.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, the answer is yes, companies can continue to approach the SME Centres.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In fact, we expect the SME Centres and TACs to play an even more significant role as we move forward with various initiatives.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: With the formation of Enterprise Singapore, we expect this process to become even more efficient and effective.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Certainly, one of Enterprise Singapore's priorities will be to see how it can better interface with the business community and specific enterprises.

speaker: Mr Speaker
